confirmed: Current production token bytes exactly equal original tested token minus an appended cfg(test) module declaration.
The original strict case reached successful allowed-root operations and an outside physical read, then outside write/create PermissionDenied and outside file/directory removal success.
Production token same-descriptor AccessCheck denied outside DELETE but allowed parent FILE_DELETE_CHILD.

Full-restricting control copies the actual restricting SID multiset, original default DACL and original SeChangeNotify privilege, omitting WRITE_RESTRICTED only; it denies outside read and DELETE_CHILD in AccessCheck.
Full-restricting control is not impersonated for filesystem I/O; do not label its read result a physical read.
The current direct legacy constructor accepts no paths/read authorities or independent operation-mediation handle.
Current elevated runner uses the same token family, while setup grants selected roots; its IPC is spawn/stdio/control, not mediation of each native file operation.
limits: No new native Windows execution, current-head qualification, permission experiment, CI rerun or ref mutation.
Observed access-mask behavior is bound to the original actual Windows run; no private Windows implementation or all-version proof.
No proof that every possible Windows isolation mechanism is impossible.
MIC is a possible separate mechanism but existing inspected chain has no root-label/token-integrity setup; original evidence does not contain object SACL or token IL observations.
No safe use of existing elevated routing as proof that the broad-ACE attack is fixed.
No blanket Err, changed expected result, skipped test, dropped outside read or reintroduced broad capability is accepted as closure.

separate read-only capability with verified read/execute grants
actual loader/IPC prerequisites with object and lifetime custody

must_retain: host four-cell controls and exact handle/object identity
public ACL query and repeat-repair booleans
full logs/XML/all attempts with source/cache/retry identities
